hook.text: In 1800s England, white moths blended into pale trees. Then factories blackened the bark. Dark moths took over.

buildup.text: Soot killed lichen, exposing dark bark. White moths became visible to birds. Dark variants survived and bred.

discovery.text: When pollution laws cleaned the air, lichen returned. White moths made a comeback. Selection reversed in decades.

twist.text: The peppered moth story was questioned in the 1990s over methodology. New experiments in 2012 confirmed it was real.

climax.text: The dark color came from a transposon insertion. A jumping gene literally changed the moth's appearance.

punchline.text: Pollution selected for dark moths. Clean air brought back the light.

quiz.question: What caused dark moths to become more common in industrial England?
options: Soot darkened trees, making white moths visible to predators
